name: Addison
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Addison, TX 2026
seo_description: Addison Aglow tree lighting and drone show, Storytime with Mrs. Claus, Elf Jr., The Polar Express dollar movie and more kids' Christmas events in Addison.
lede: The story of Christmas in Addison is a young one: the town lights its tree in Addison Circle Park and, in 2026, turns all of December into A Merry Month of Everything, headlined by Addison Aglow and the town's first holiday drone show. Down the road, Vitruvian Lights wraps Vitruvian Park in lights each season, in a town that began in 1902 as a Cotton Belt railroad junction.
sections: Addison Aglow and A Merry Month of Everything, new for 2026

For 2026 the Town of Addison turned December into A Merry Month of Everything, with something planned almost every day, Visit Addison says. Lit Night Projections by Lightware Labs light up the Addison water tower, the magnolia trees, the face of The Addison Performing Arts Centre and part of Town Hall each night, CW33 reported. The centerpiece is Addison Aglow in Addison Circle Park, where the 32 foot tree is lit at 6 pm and the town's first holiday drone show follows at 8 pm. The plan includes a s'mores station, arts and crafts, mini train rides and photos with Santa.

Addison's other big light show glows along the creek in Vitruvian Park at 3966 Vitruvian Way. For the 2025 season the town's event page said the tree lights would come on daily from 5 to 11 pm starting Sunday, November 23, with a 3D walk through gift box lit with LEDs for holiday photos. For 2026 Visit Addison lists the switch being flipped on November 28 at 6 pm, with a party band, food trucks, free photos with Santa, an elf balloon artist and Letters to Santa with Mrs. Claus. Event parking is $15, and the town's 2025 page said nearby apartment communities do not allow event parking.
How a Cotton Belt junction became Addison

Addison started with a railroad. Landowner S. S. Noell gave land so the Cotton Belt would build its line to Dallas through the area, the town says, and the stop was called Noell Junction. The Handbook of Texas records a depot there in 1902 and a spur to Dallas in 1903; until 1917 residents rode into Dallas on the Plug, a little train of one engine, a coal tender and a passenger car. Since Texas already had a Noell, the 1904 post office took the name of Addison Robertson. Today DART's Silver Line follows the old Cotton Belt, with an Addison Station at 4925 Arapaho Road.
celebrates: Addison celebrates in a small area packed with things to do. In 2026 the town filled December with A Merry Month of Everything: nightly projections on the water tower and Town Hall, Addison Aglow with a tree lighting and drone show in Addison Circle Park, Storytime with Mrs. Claus at the Stone Cottage, and a run of holiday shows at The Addison Performing Arts Centre, from Elf Jr. and A Charlie Brown Christmas to handbell concerts and $1 Christmas movies. Vitruvian Lights brightens Vitruvian Park, and kids can drop letters to Santa at the Java and Hopps pavilion.
lastyear: In 2025 the Addison Circle Holiday Tree Lighting was planned for Friday, December 5, from 6 to 9 pm, with Mayor Bruce Arfsten lighting the town's Christmas tree, according to the Town of Addison's event listing. Over in Vitruvian Park, the town's Vitruvian Lights page said the tree lights would be on daily from 5 to 11 pm starting Sunday, November 23, with a lighted 3D walk through gift box for family photos.
facts: Addison was first called Noell Junction after S. S. Noell, whose family home sat on 1,200 acres south of Belt Line Road. The town took its name in 1904 from Addison Robertson, a local carpenter and Civil War veteran. Addison incorporated in 1953, and Addison Airport opened in 1956, the Handbook of Texas says. The town grew from 595 residents in 1970 to 14,166 in 2000.
trains: Trains are part of Addison's story from the start: the Cotton Belt depot at Noell Junction opened in 1902, and the Plug carried riders to Dallas from 1903 to 1917. DART's Silver Line now runs along the old Cotton Belt corridor with an Addison Station at 4925 Arapaho Road; DART listed its opening as late 2025 to mid 2026. The Cotton Belt Trail is being built alongside. For a train day out, the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano, the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco and the M-Line Trolley in Dallas are close by.

kidfact: Long ago, people in Addison rode to Dallas on a tiny train nicknamed the Plug, which had just one engine, one coal car and one passenger car, the Handbook of Texas says.
faq: Addison Aglow, the town's official tree lighting, is in Addison Circle Park in early December. The 32 foot tree is lit at 6 pm, and the evening ends with Addison's first holiday drone show at 8 pm. Visit Addison lists it as free, with crafts, a s'mores station, mini train rides and photos with Santa planned.

There are two main places. Vitruvian Lights covers the trees of Vitruvian Park on Vitruvian Way, and the town's Lit Night Projections by Lightware Labs shine on the water tower, Town Hall, the magnolia trees and The Addison Performing Arts Centre each night in December. Addison Circle Park has the town Christmas tree.
How did Addison get its name?

The town grew up around a Cotton Belt railroad stop called Noell Junction, named for landowner S. S. Noell. When a post office opened in 1904, Texas already had a town called Noell, so the community took the name of Addison Robertson, a local carpenter and Civil War veteran, the Town of Addison says.
Can you take the train to Addison?

DART's Silver Line follows the old Cotton Belt railroad through town and has an Addison Station at 4925 Arapaho Road, close to Addison Circle. DART listed the line's opening as late 2025 to mid 2026, so check DART for current service before planning a holiday trip by rail.
Are there Christmas shows for kids in Addison?

Yes. The Addison Performing Arts Centre hosts the town's holiday stage lineup, which in 2026 includes Elf Jr. by Rockwall Acting, A Charlie Brown Christmas by Accolade, Dorothy Shaw Bell Choir concerts and $1 Christmas Movie Festival screenings, all listed on Visit Addison's holiday page.
